subject: Commercial onboarding: PO vs corporate card + vendor onboarding constraints
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@summithealth.com>, Marcus Liu <marcus.liu@summithealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Commercial onboarding: PO vs corporate card + vendor onboarding constraints

Great to meet this morning — quick recap and questions so we can align procurement and finance expectations on both sides. TL;DR: Summit needs vendor onboarding + AP gating; we can pilot on card if limits allow, otherwise PO for pilot.

Recap from call:
- Pilot scope: 3-month inference pilot (up to 250k tokens/day) for two internal product teams.
- Commercial ask: proof of concept billing + a pathway to production (month-to-month to start).
- Main gating items flagged by Summit: supplier portal registration, vendor taxonomy & tax docs, PO vs P-card decision, and SOW/MSA sign-off path.

Clarifying questions (can you confirm?):
1) Does Summit require a PO for any transaction > $10k, or is the threshold $25k? We want to know whether the pilot (estimated $18k/month) will require a PO right away.
2) Is P-card accepted for multi-month pilots if the card limit is raised, or does AP insist on PO for recurring services?
3) Which supplier portal (Coupa/SAP Ariba/ProcOps) should we register with? Any required supplier code we need to include on the invoice?
4) Are there any additional evidence items for onboarding besides W-9 (US) and COI (insurance)? For example, do you need a SOC2 or security questionnaire to kick off vendor registration?
5) Who will generate the PO (ProcOps) and who should we expect as the AP contact for billing questions?

Proposed next steps (owner):
- Karthik: provide SOW draft and rate card (attached: Redwood_SOW_draft_v2.pdf) — today EOD.
- Lauren: share finance contact and sample invoice format.
- Ben: confirm billing cadence and whether Redwood can accept monthly invoices + Net30.
- Elena/Marcus: confirm PO threshold and supplier portal.

Attachments: Redwood_SOW_draft_v2.pdf (SOW + rate card)

Thanks — simple asks so procurement can move the pilot to PO or card-based billing.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
(karthik@redwoodinference.com)
From: Elena Park <elena.park@summithealth.com>

Cc: ProcOps Team <procops@summithealth.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commercial onboarding: PO vs corporate card + vendor onboarding constraints

Thanks for the recap and the SOW, Karthik. A few specifics from AP/procurement side that will determine whether we route this via P-card or PO: 

Key constraints:
- PO threshold: Summit requires a Purchase Order for multi-month services when expected spend > $15,000/month or $30,000 total commitment. (Pilot estimated at ~$18k/month — this will typically be PO'd.)
- P-card: our P-card program can be used for one-off purchases up to $7,500 per transaction. Cards are not usually used for recurring SaaS subscriptions unless Procurement approves an exception.
- Supplier portal: we use Coupa plus an internal ProcOps intake. Vendor registration requires:
  - Completed supplier form in Coupa (fields: legal name, EIN, remit address)
  - W-9 (or W-8 for non-US), COI (ins cert), bank ACH details (or remit address for checks)
  - Security attestation: short questionnaire (not full SOC2) for pilots; SOC2 is required for production with PHI/PII scope.
- PO format: PO must include vendor legal name and the assigned Summit supplier ID; ProcOps will issue the PO once vendor registration is approved.

Attachments: I attached the Summit AP checklist (Summit_AP_Checklist.pdf) and our PO template. Please note ProcOps will not issue a PO until the supplier profile is fully completed.

Timeline expectations:
- If you complete Coupa registration and return the requested docs this week, ProcOps can route for approval next Tue (4/6). If approved, PO generation typically takes 3–5 business days.
- If you prefer P-card, we would need a one-time charge under $7.5k and Procurement approval for any exception to use card for recurring billing.

Next steps we need from Redwood:
1) Complete supplier registration (Coupa) — I will send the invite once you confirm legal name and EIN.
2) Confirm whether Redwood can accept Net30 invoices and provide ACH details for payment.
3) Confirm whether you want us to route a PO for the estimated pilot spend.

Happy to hop on a short follow-up with ProcOps if helpful.

— Elena Park
Director, Procurement Operations | Summit Health
(elena.park@summithealth.com)

Thanks Elena — a couple notes from Redwood finance side: 
- Billing cadence: Redwood can invoice monthly, Net30 by default. We can consider Net15 for pilot if that helps speed approvals, but we'd need to lock that in on the SOW.
- Payment methods: we accept ACH (preferred), wire, and corporate card. To use card for the pilot we'd need a ProcOps exception to raise the per-transaction limit, or you can split the first month into multiple card transactions (not ideal).
- Tax/Vendor setup: please confirm the exact EIN/legal name that Coupa will expect — we'll match exactly to avoid delays.

Quick ask: can you share the ProcOps contact email so we can route registration documents directly? Also, if ProcOps issues the PO, please confirm whether the PO will reference the HubSpot deal ID (SD-2027-1179) — that helps our AR team reconcile invoices quickly.

— Ben Carter
Finance Ops, Redwood Inference

Appreciate the detail here. Quick confirmations from procurement: 

- We'll push for a PO for the pilot given the ~$18k/month estimate. ProcOps needs the completed Coupa registration + W-9 + COI + proof of insurance to create supplier profile.
- We can accelerate onboarding if Redwood signs our standard MSA (I'll send the doc link) and provides the COI — ProcOps generally clears new suppliers faster with a signed MSA.
- I'll attach the Summit PO template so your SOW/invoice matches the required fields (Summit_PO_Template.docx). Please ensure the invoice includes: Summit supplier ID (to be assigned), Redwood legal name, EIN, and HubSpot deal reference (SD-2027-1179).

Action items from Procure: 
1) Karthik — please confirm legal name and EIN for Coupa invite.
2) Karthik/Ben — confirm whether Redwood will accept Net30 (we're fine with Net30).
3) Lauren — once supplier ID assigned, share with Redwood AR.
4) Marcus — I'll escalate MSA to legal and request ProcOps to queue the PO once documents arrive.

If you can get the Coupa registration in today, ProcOps will attempt approval on Tue 4/6 and we can have a PO by mid-next-week. Happy to jump on a 15m call with ProcOps if that helps.

— Marcus Liu
Procurement Manager | Summit Health
(marcus.liu@summithealth.com)
